solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What burglars use as the last resort

indicators.note: to resort is to sort again, so the letters of the two words beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A burglar reaches for some trick only when every other option has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last resort' reads as a set phrase, but 'resort' is the anagram signal working on THE LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Burglars rely on moving quietly and unseen, which is what this word for secrecy of movement names.

clue.text: A young bird that's … well … yellow!

parts.note: a spring is a well, a source of water
yellow means cowardly, as does chicken

explanation.surface: A baby bird is, well, yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like hesitation but is a water source; 'yellow' is cowardly, not the colour of chicks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means a young fowl, though now mostly used for a youthful person.

clue.text: "All together" possibly means the Home Counties

indicators.note: possibly means the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England, SE

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether a phrase refers to the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties bordering London, in England's south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived phrase means as a single body, everyone at once.

clue.text: Does he set the standard for happiness?

definitions.text: Does he set the standard for happiness?

parts.words: Does he set the standard for happiness
parts.note: the British idiom as happy as this man makes him the yardstick of contentment

explanation.surface: A question about who is the measure of being happy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'happy as Larry' means extremely happy, so this man is the benchmark.

clue.text: Sharp turns needed to secure locks

definitions.meaning: very tight bends in a road
pins that hold hair in place, locks being tresses

explanation.surface: Tricky manoeuvres are required to fasten some locks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both tight U-shaped road bends and the U-shaped pins holding hair.

clue.text: Some pop a question that's not clear

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is nervously popping the question, but their proposal comes out muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something you cannot see through, literally or figuratively, is unclear: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Admit to being a priest

parts.note: reads as confessing one's calling, but means formally admitting someone into the priesthood

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that they are a member of the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop confers holy orders, formally making someone a priest.

clue.text: Beautiful virgin of myth also roamed freely

parts.note: and means also

indicators.note: freely means the letters move about loosely

explanation.surface: A lovely maiden from legend who also wandered at will.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the princess was chained to a rock for a sea monster and rescued by Perseus.

clue.text: Sinister supporter of royal escutcheon

parts.note: in heraldry sinister is the left side, and the Scottish beast stands there holding up the British royal arms

explanation.surface: An evil-sounding backer of the royal coat of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' is the heraldic term for left, not wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: The British royal arms have a lion on the left as viewed and a horned beast on the heraldic left.

clue.text: Demonstrated nuptially the triumph of hope over experience?

definitions.text: Demonstrated nuptially the triumph of hope over experience?

parts.words: Demonstrated nuptially the triumph of hope over experience
parts.note: Samuel Johnson called a second marriage the triumph of hope over experience, so someone who showed it at a wedding wed again

explanation.surface: A quotation about optimism winning out over hard lessons, shown at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson's quip was about a man marrying a second time, so acting it out means wedding once more.

clue.text: Boring bit of exercise

definitions.meaning: a tool or bit that bores holes
a routine practice session, as in a fire practice or military training

explanation.surface: Someone finds one part of their workout tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' means dull on the surface but means making holes here.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a hole-making tool and a repetitive training routine.

clue.text: Get cold feet having no bottle

definitions.meaning: become too frightened to go ahead
bottle is British slang for courage, so lacking it

explanation.surface: Someone panics when the drink runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing courage at the last moment is what both getting cold feet and lacking bottle mean.

clue.text: Negative and affirmative backing is most curious

parts.note: no is a negative reply

indicators.note: backing means the word for affirmative is read backwards

parts.note: yes is an affirmative reply

explanation.surface: Someone says no and then backs yes, which is very odd behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reads as supporting, but here it turns the reply round.
explanation.definitionFit: Prying and inquisitive, a person very curious about others' affairs is described by this informal adjective.

clue.text: French peas we arranged around duck — very nasty!

indicators.note: around means the two French words are placed either side of the duck

parts.note: pois is French for peas
nous is French for we, still under the French of the clue
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A French dish of peas arranged around duck turns out to be thoroughly unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' carries over to both 'peas' and 'we'; 'arranged' just links the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something toxic or venomous is harmful, and figuratively the word describes very nasty, spiteful behaviour.

clue.text: Timid queen said to be associated with 19

indicators.note: said means the two words are spoken and the sound gives the entry

parts.note: timid means shy, and Queen Anne is the queen

explanation.surface: A shy monarch is reportedly linked with a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is COMANCHE: both are Native American peoples of the Great Plains.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are Plains tribes of North America, so one is naturally associated with the other.

clue.text: A little one may have voted for Brexit

definitions.text: A little one may have voted for Brexit

parts.words: A little one may have voted for Brexit
parts.note: a Little ... is an insular, inward-looking Briton, the type expected to vote Leave

explanation.surface: A child might have cast a vote to leave the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little one' suggests a child; with Little before it the answer names an insular English nationalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A Little Englander opposes foreign involvement, the outlook associated with the Brexit vote.

clue.text: Shed a pound at one work-out

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

indicators.note: a work-out exercises and reshapes, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone loses a pound in weight at a single gym session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a verb of losing weight but is the noun for a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple shed or hut built against a wall, its roof sloping one way, is this kind of structure.

clue.text: Mere existence, of interest to anglers naturally

parts.note: a mere is a small lake or pond
life means existence

explanation.surface: Simply being alive is, of course, something fishermen care about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' looks like 'only' but is a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish, insects and plants of still water are what anglers study and depend on.

clue.text: One almost impatient to catch cold in this period

indicators.note: to catch means the letters close round the cold one

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: eager means keen and impatient
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone nearly impatient to catch a cold during this time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final letter of the impatient word; 'to catch' sets the cold letter just after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacial epoch is a long era in Earth's history, a period of geological time.

clue.text: Medicine prepared without one for such diseases

indicators.note: prepared means the letters of medicine are worked up afresh, without the one left out

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A remedy made up without one ingredient for certain illnesses.
explanation.walkthrough: MEDICINE less I leaves letters rearranged by 'prepared'.
explanation.definitionFit: Diseases regularly found in a particular region or people are described with this adjective.

clue.text: Indian love story about hospital with Charlie as Romeo

indicators.note: with Charlie as Romeo means one letter stands in place of the other
about means the love story goes round the hospital letter

parts.note: a romance is a love story
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tale of love set around a hospital, with someone called Charlie playing Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with Charlie as Romeo' swaps the R of ROMANCE for C.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American people of the southern plains, called Indian in older usage.

clue.text: Appropriate kind of clue for this answer?

definitions.text: Appropriate kind of clue for this answer?

parts.words: Appropriate kind of clue for this answer
parts.note: the puzzle itself is the kind with puzzling clues, so the answer names its own type

explanation.surface: A question about which style of clue best suits this solution.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzling, obscure clues like these are the kind this crossword uses, which is self-referential.

clue.text: What orthographer does for short intervals

definitions.meaning: an orthographer is expert in correct writing of words
brief periods of time, as in a spell of rain

explanation.surface: A question about what a spelling expert does in brief breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the act of writing words letter by letter and brief periods of time.

clue.text: A child dozed off in this Highland odyssey

parts.note: a kid is a child
napped means dozed off

explanation.surface: A child falls asleep while being read a Scottish adventure story.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's novel follows David Balfour on a journey across the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Respected leader of party with money abroad

parts.note: a do is a party
the yen is Japan's currency, money from abroad

explanation.surface: A distinguished figure leads a party with funds overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The most senior, respected member of a group is its leading elder figure.

clue.text: Dismal day on train

parts.note: to rear is to bring up or train

explanation.surface: A gloomy day spent on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway but is a verb meaning bring up.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic and poetic word for gloomy or bleak, synonymous with dreary.

clue.text: A traveller starts to notice our manners are different

indicators.note: starts to means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A visitor begins to see that local customs differ from home.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no settled home moves from place to place, so is a traveller.

clue.text: Queen's favourite cheese

definitions.meaning: Robert Dudley, Earl of ..., was the favourite courtier of Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: The monarch's preferred cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Leicester is an orange English cheese named after the Midlands county.
explanation.definitionFit: The earl was Elizabeth I's favourite, and the county also names a hard cheese.

clue.text: Men in black have trouble with spooks

indicators.note: have means the men hold the trouble between them

parts.note: the SS, the Nazi paramilitary force, wore black uniforms
care means worry or trouble

explanation.surface: Black-clad agents run into difficulty with spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spooks' suggests spies but is a verb meaning frightens.
explanation.definitionFit: To spook someone is to frighten them, a direct synonym in the third person.

clue.text: A race he organised would keep you awake

indicators.note: organised means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A man arranges a race that is so noisy it keeps you up.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful ache in the ear is the kind of complaint that stops a person sleeping.
